job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: Today in our science lab, we explored how we see the world. We started by looking at a wall and a mirror. Even though the wall is rough, it reflects light in many directions, which is why we can see it from any angle. Next, we examined a model of the human eye. We learned that the cornea acts as the primary lens, bending light significantly before it even reaches the internal crystalline lens. This internal lens is not made of glass; it is a flexible, living tissue that changes its shape to focus on objects at different distances. We also discussed how light enters the eye and hits the retina, where specialized cells work together. Cones are responsible for detecting colors in bright light, while rods are sensitive to dim light. Finally, we talked about vision health. While carrots are a great source of Vitamin A, they are not the only way to maintain healthy eyes; leafy greens and dairy are also vital. We concluded that vision is a complex process where light enters the eye, rather than our eyes sending out rays to touch objects. Understanding these mechanisms helps us appreciate how our eyes function and why we must protect them from strain and poor nutrition.

items.evidence: Even though the wall is rough, it reflects light in many directions, which is why we can see it from any angle.
items.q: Why can we see a rough wall from any spot in the room?
options: It bounces light back in all directions
It does not reflect light, only mirrors do
It catches the rays our eyes send out
It reflects light straight back in one direction
items.explain: A rough wall reflects light in many directions, so light reaches our eyes from any angle.

wrong.why: thinks rough objects do not reflect light
thinks eyes send out rays to see
mixes up a wall with a mirror

items.evidence: We learned that the cornea acts as the primary lens, bending light significantly before it even reaches the internal crystalline lens.
items.q: How does the cornea help us see?
options: It bends light strongly before the inner lens
It only covers the eye and bends nothing
It changes its shape to focus near and far
It picks up colours when light is bright
items.explain: The cornea is the main lens; it bends light a lot before light reaches the inner lens.

wrong.why: thinks the cornea only protects the eye
mixes up the cornea with the inner lens
mixes up the cornea with cone cells

items.evidence: This internal lens is not made of glass; it is a flexible, living tissue that changes its shape to focus on objects at different distances.
items.q: Meera looks up from her book to a far tree. What does her eye's lens do?
options: The lens, being living tissue, alters its shape
The lens, being glass, stays rigid and fixed
The lens slides forward and back like a camera
The lens stays still while the cornea refocuses
items.explain: The eye's lens is flexible living tissue that changes shape to focus at different distances.

wrong.why: thinks the lens is rigid glass
thinks the eye focuses like a camera

items.evidence: Cones are responsible for detecting colors in bright light, while rods are sensitive to dim light.
items.q: In a nearly dark room, which retina cells help Aman see most?
options: Rods, because they work in weak light
Cones, because they sense every colour
Rods and cones, because both see colours
Neither, because eyes send out rays instead
items.explain: Rods are sensitive to dim light; cones detect colours only in bright light.

wrong.why: picks cones as the more famous cells
thinks rods and cones both see colours
thinks eyes send out rays to see

items.evidence: While carrots are a great source of Vitamin A, they are not the only way to maintain healthy eyes; leafy greens and dairy are also vital.
items.q: Sana dislikes carrots. How can she still keep her eyes healthy?
options: By having green vegetables and milk products
By eating carrots anyway, the only true source
By resting her eyes, since food does not matter
By checking she can still see far stars
items.explain: Carrots are not the only way; leafy greens and dairy are also vital for healthy eyes.

wrong.why: thinks carrots are the only source of Vitamin A
ignores that poor nutrition harms eyes
thinks seeing stars proves eyes are healthy
